Theme

Money, work & business · Town, shops & places

haggle verb

also haggling, bargain over the price, haggle over the price, beat down the price

classical

Suet. Gram. 7.2: nec unquam dē mercēdibus pactus, he never bargained over his fees
Plaut. Bacch. 865–866: pacīscī cum illō paululā pecūniā potes, you can strike a bargain with him for a little money

dē pretiō pacīscī

verb phrase: pacīscor, deponent

bargain over the price, haggle

pacīscor is to bargain, to settle terms (with long ī, de Vaan 452, pacīscere); once buyer and seller agree, dē pretiō convēnit (Quint. 4.2.41).

Other words

  • nūndinor, nūndinārī, nūndinātus sum — haggle, chaffer (with contempt)

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Liv. 22.56.3: in captīvōrum pretiīs … nec magnī ducis mōre nūndinantem, haggling over the prisoners’ ransoms, not as a great general would

    Properly to trade at the market (nūndinae, with long ū, de Vaan 415); said with contempt of haggling, and of trafficking in what should not be sold (Cic. Phil. 3.10, Lewis & Short).

  • licitor, licitārī, licitātus sum — bid, make an offer

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Plaut. Merc. 441: nē licitēre advorsum meī animī sententiam, don’t go bidding against my wishes; Comen. OP 126: Ēmptor licitātur, et pretium offert

    In Plautus to bid against a rival buyer; Comenius uses it of the customer making his offer at a stall.

Examples

  • In portum vēnī, nāvem prōspexī, quantī veheret interrogāvī, dē pretiō convēnit, cōnscendī, sublātae sunt ancorae, solvimus ōram, profectī sumus.

    I came to the harbour, looked over a ship, asked what the fare was, we agreed on the price, I went aboard, the anchors were weighed, we cast off and set out.Quint. 4.2.41

  • praetereā cōmī facilīque nātūrā, nec unquam dē mercēdibus pactus, eōque plūra ex līberālitāte discentium cōnsecūtus

    a kindly, easy-going man besides, who never bargained over his fees and so received all the more from his pupils’ generositySuet. Gram. 7.2

  • Vēnditor ostentat rem prōmercālem, et indicat pretium, quantī liceat. Ēmptor licitātur, et pretium offert.

    The seller shows his goods and names the price, what they cost; the buyer bargains and offers a price.Comen. OP 126

See also price, bargain, market, buy, sell, set a price.

SourcesLewis & Short: paciscor · Lewis & Short: nundinor · Lewis & Short: licitor
